Hoffman et al. (2026) frame the observed PSD as a transport-filtered distribution. A simple diagnostic is the capture fraction *f*(*d*, δ) = 1 − exp(−*w*~s~(*d*)·δ / *K*) and the critical size where *w*~s~(*d*)·δ / *K* ≈ 1. The calculation below uses Stokes settling/rise speed with user-supplied `delta_m` = `r hoffman_delta_m` m and `K_m2_s` = `r hoffman_K_m2_s` m^2/s. These are assumptions, not measured site parameters, and should be replaced with field-specific values before a mechanistic transport correction is attempted.

```{r hoffman-critical-size-piecewise}
matrix_fit_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  Matrix = c("River water", "Sediment", "Ocean water"),
  cpsd_fit = list(cpsd_fit_all, cpsd_fit_sed_all, cpsd_fit_ocean_all),
  median_density_g_cm3 = c(
    median(raw_particles_river$density_g_cm3, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(raw_particles_sed$density_g_cm3, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(raw_particles_ocean$density_g_cm3, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  water_density_g_cm3 = c(1.00, 1.00, 1.025)
)

critical_piecewise_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(matrix_fit_tbl)), function(i) {
  fit_i <- matrix_fit_tbl$cpsd_fit[[i]]
  dc_i <- estimate_critical_size(
    delta_m = hoffman_delta_m,
    K_m2_s = hoffman_K_m2_s,
    density_g_cm3 = matrix_fit_tbl$median_density_g_cm3[i],
    water_density_g_cm3 = matrix_fit_tbl$water_density_g_cm3[i]
  )
  pw_i <- piecewise_cpsd_diagnostic(fit_i)
  tibble::tibble(
    Matrix = matrix_fit_tbl$Matrix[i],
    median_density_g_cm3 = matrix_fit_tbl$median_density_g_cm3[i],
    critical_size_um = dc_i,
    fit_lod_low_um = fit_i$lower_lod_used_um,
    fit_lod_high_um = fit_i$upper_lod_um,
    straddles_critical_size = is.finite(dc_i) && dc_i >= fit_i$lower_lod_used_um && dc_i <= fit_i$upper_lod_um,
    single_a_cpsd = fit_i$a_cpsd,
    single_a_psd = fit_i$a_psd,
    piecewise_break_um = pw_i$break_um,
    piecewise_low_a_cpsd = pw_i$slope_low,
    piecewise_high_a_cpsd = pw_i$slope_high,
    piecewise_delta_aic = pw_i$delta_aic
  )
}))

knitr::kable(
  critical_piecewise_tbl,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "SPEC 4 diagnostic: critical size and two-segment C-PSD fit by matrix"
)
```

The piecewise fits are diagnostic only. A fit window that straddles the assumed critical size is flagged because the fitted single slope may blend a transport-distorted fine-size regime with the coarser-size regime. Per Hoffman et al. (2026), future refinement should prioritize measured 3-D geometry and polymer density over increasingly elaborate settling equations; even precise-geometry settling models retain substantial residual error, so settling-based corrections should be treated as bias-level adjustments rather than high-precision concentration estimates.

## 13.3 Piecewise (dual-slope) PSD as a bounding exposure case

The production `correction_factor()` extrapolates a single fitted power-law slope from the measured LOD window down to the 1 um target floor. The two-segment diagnostic above (§13.2) shows the data themselves often prefer a shallower fine-size slope below a break point and a steeper coarse-size slope above it (river ΔAIC in the diagnostic table strongly favors the two-segment model; sediment likewise). Because the sub-floor extrapolation zone (1 um to the fitted LOD) can straddle or sit near that break — and because the fitted critical size `d_c` for river (~36 um) falls inside that 1-50 um extrapolation zone rather than inside the fit window itself — a single coarse slope may not be the right model to extrapolate through that zone. Independent evidence that single power laws mis-extrapolate to small, unmeasured sizes: in the St Louis Estuary, a single power law extrapolated to 1.3-12 particles/L for 5-5000 um while flow cytometry directly measured 600-1,600 particles/L in the same system ([Thomas et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.3c10776)), and [Segur et al. (2026)](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-8524083/v1) find size-aligned 1-5000 um concentrations average ~600x higher than reported values based on single-slope extrapolation. Both are cited as **evidence that single-power-law extrapolation to small sizes is unreliable in general**, not as a validated correction for this dataset.

`correction_factor_piecewise()` (`R/mp_risk_utils.R`, SPEC 2b) implements the two-segment alternative: it integrates dN/dL = k*L^a using the fine-segment differential slope over [1, break_um] and the coarse-segment differential slope over [break_um, 5000], with the coarse segment's density scaled so the two segments meet exactly (are continuous) at `break_um`. The piecewise cumulative slopes from the §13.2 diagnostic are converted to the differential convention (a_psd = a_cpsd - 1) internally via `slope_convention = "cumulative"`, consistent with the SPEC 1c guard. **This is a labeled bounding sensitivity, not a replacement for the single-slope production CF** — the production exposure pipeline (Sections 5-6, 9-10, 12) is unchanged. The 1 um-LOD_low sub-window is unconstrained by data in *both* the single-slope and piecewise case; the piecewise result quantifies structural (model-form) uncertainty in how that unconstrained sub-window is extrapolated, which is not captured by the Gaussian `slope_structural_sd` already added to the fit-uncertainty propagation.

```{r spec2b-piecewise-cf}
piecewise_cf_row <- function(matrix_label, piecewise_row, L_meas_min, L_meas_max) {
  brk <- piecewise_row$piecewise_break_um
  s_lo <- piecewise_row$piecewise_low_a_cpsd
  s_hi <- piecewise_row$piecewise_high_a_cpsd
  if (!is.finite(brk) || !is.finite(s_lo) || !is.finite(s_hi)) {
    return(tibble::tibble(Matrix = matrix_label, break_um = NA_real_, cf_piecewise = NA_real_))
  }
  cf_pw <- correction_factor_piecewise(
    a_low = s_lo, a_high = s_hi, break_um = brk,
    L_meas_min = L_meas_min, L_meas_max = L_meas_max,
    L_tar_min = 1, L_tar_max = 5000,
    slope_convention = "cumulative"
  )
  tibble::tibble(Matrix = matrix_label, break_um = brk, cf_piecewise = cf_pw)
}

pw_river <- piecewise_cf_row("River water", dplyr::filter(critical_piecewise_tbl, Matrix == "River water"), L_meas_min_use, L_meas_max_use)
pw_sed   <- piecewise_cf_row("Sediment",    dplyr::filter(critical_piecewise_tbl, Matrix == "Sediment"),    L_meas_min_use_sed, L_meas_max_use_sed)
pw_ocean <- piecewise_cf_row("Ocean water", dplyr::filter(critical_piecewise_tbl, Matrix == "Ocean water"), L_meas_min_ocean, L_meas_max_ocean)

# Piecewise sensitivity is an exposure-only (CF/EED) effect: apply the single
# piecewise CF point estimate to the raw per-sample measured concentrations,
# then bootstrap the EED exactly as for the single-slope case. Hazard (haz*)
# is unchanged, so any RQ shift below is attributable to the piecewise CF alone.
set.seed(9401)
eed_boot_piecewise_river <- if (is.finite(pw_river$cf_piecewise)) {
  bootstrap_eed(monitoring$C_measured_pL * pw_river$cf_piecewise, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95))
} else NULL
set.seed(9402)
eed_boot_piecewise_sed <- if (is.finite(pw_sed$cf_piecewise)) {
  bootstrap_eed(monitoring_sed$C_measured_pkg * pw_sed$cf_piecewise, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95))
} else NULL
set.seed(9403)
eed_boot_piecewise_ocean <- if (is.finite(pw_ocean$cf_piecewise)) {
  bootstrap_eed(monitoring_ocean$C_measured_pL * pw_ocean$cf_piecewise, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95))
} else NULL

set.seed(9411)
risk_summary_piecewise_river <- if (!is.null(eed_boot_piecewise_river)) {
  summarize_rq(draw_rq_mc1d(haz, eed_boot_piecewise_river$q50, n_risk = n_risk))
} else NULL
set.seed(9412)
risk_summary_piecewise_sed <- if (!is.null(eed_boot_piecewise_sed)) {
  summarize_rq(draw_rq_mc1d(haz_sed, eed_boot_piecewise_sed$q50, n_risk = n_risk_sed))
} else NULL
set.seed(9413)
risk_summary_piecewise_ocean <- if (!is.null(eed_boot_piecewise_ocean)) {
  summarize_rq(draw_rq_mc1d(haz_ocean, eed_boot_piecewise_ocean$q50, n_risk = n_risk_ocean))
} else NULL
```

```{r spec2b-bounding-table}
cf_bounding_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(Matrix = "River water", break_um = pw_river$break_um,
                 CF_single_slope_p50 = median(combined_cf), CF_piecewise = pw_river$cf_piecewise,
                 EED_single_slope_q50 = median(eed_boot$q50),
                 EED_piecewise_q50 = if (!is.null(eed_boot_piecewise_river)) median(eed_boot_piecewise_river$q50) else NA_real_),
  tibble::tibble(Matrix = "Sediment", break_um = pw_sed$break_um,
                 CF_single_slope_p50 = median(combined_cf_sed), CF_piecewise = pw_sed$cf_piecewise,
                 EED_single_slope_q50 = median(eed_boot_sed$q50),
                 EED_piecewise_q50 = if (!is.null(eed_boot_piecewise_sed)) median(eed_boot_piecewise_sed$q50) else NA_real_),
  tibble::tibble(Matrix = "Ocean water", break_um = pw_ocean$break_um,
                 CF_single_slope_p50 = median(combined_cf_ocean), CF_piecewise = pw_ocean$cf_piecewise,
                 EED_single_slope_q50 = median(eed_boot_ocean$q50),
                 EED_piecewise_q50 = if (!is.null(eed_boot_piecewise_ocean)) median(eed_boot_piecewise_ocean$q50) else NA_real_)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(CF_ratio_piecewise_vs_single = CF_piecewise / CF_single_slope_p50)

knitr::kable(
  cf_bounding_tbl, digits = 3,
  caption = "SPEC 2b: single-slope (production) vs. piecewise (bounding sensitivity) correction factor and EED, by matrix"
)
```

**Bounding range interpretation.** The table above states, per matrix, the single-slope production RQ alongside the piecewise-sensitivity RQ; whichever is larger sets the upper bound of the sensitivity range and whichever is smaller sets the lower bound. Because the fine-size (sub-break) slope from the §13.2 diagnostic is shallower than the coarse-size slope for the matrices where the two-segment model is favored, the piecewise CF is expected to sit *below* the single-slope CF (less extrapolated mass assigned to the unconstrained 1 um-LOD_low zone) — i.e., the piecewise bound is expected to **narrow** the exposure (and therefore RQ) estimate relative to the single-slope production value, not widen it, for this dataset. This is stated as an expectation to be read against the rendered numbers above, not assumed; if a matrix's piecewise CF instead exceeds the single-slope CF, that reversal is itself informative about how sensitive the conclusion is to the extrapolation model and should be flagged rather than averaged away. Regardless of direction, the single-slope CF remains the production default per the guardrails in the corrective-revision spec; the piecewise result is reported here strictly as a labeled sensitivity bound. **Sediment caveat (SPEC 1d):** the Sediment column/row above is illustrative only, for the same reason noted in Section 13.1/11.3.0 — its exposure concentration is not a genuine particles/kg-dry-weight value.

`plot_rq_hist_combined()` (sourced from `R/risk_plotting.R`) row-binds the 1D Monte Carlo

alongside the River water and Ocean water rows as a comparable risk finding.**

# 12.5 Methods-robustness and source-attribution analyses (surface water only)

Three additive analyses testing whether the risk conclusion is robust to specific methodological choices (the sub-floor extrapolation, the extrapolation model itself), and whether the river-vs-ocean slope difference has independent support from polymer composition. River and ocean only — sediment is not touched. None of these change the production headline (single-slope C-PSD, `L_tar_min = 1` µm); each is a clearly-labeled sensitivity/robustness addition that reuses the already-computed production hazard/exposure objects wherever possible rather than recomputing them.

## 12.5.1 RQ sensitivity to the extrapolation floor L_tar_min (food dilution)

The production correction factor extrapolates the measured particle count down to `L_tar_min = 1` µm. Food Dilution is volume-weighted, so a power-law explosion of sub-floor particle *number* adds little particle *volume* — the RQ may be far less sensitive to `L_tar_min` than the raw number-based CF implies. This test is only valid if exposure and hazard are evaluated on the same lower size bound, so for each floor the toxicity dataset is filtered to match: a ToMEx record is excluded from a given floor if its own characteristic tested size (`size.length.um.used.for.conversions` for monodisperse records, or the tested range via `size.length.max.um.used.for.conversions` for polydisperse records — the same field `PSSDplusplus::align_data()` itself uses to size-align doses) falls entirely below that floor. Records with a missing characteristic size are excluded rather than imputed. `filter_tox_by_size_floor()` (`R/mp_risk_utils.R`) implements this rule.

At each floor, three things move together: (1) the exposure-side correction factor and EED are recomputed over `[L_tar_min, 5000]` µm; (2) the pSSD++ integration floor (`x1M_set` in `matrix_function()`, `x1D_set` in `run_pssd_pipeline()`) is set to the same `L_tar_min`; and (3) the Food Dilution toxicity records are filtered as above before the hazard alignment is re-derived. The `L_tar_min = 1` µm row reuses the already-computed production CF/EED/hazard objects rather than recomputing an identical result under a new seed (relocate-don't-recompute).

```{r m12-floor-sensitivity, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
m12_floors <- c(1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 20)

m12_run_one_floor <- function(L_tar_min, matrix_label, monitoring_df, cpsd_fit, alpha_draws,
                               tox_data_base, param_values_base, environments,
                               matrix_extra_args, rave_override_fn, seed_base,
                               prod_cf = NULL, prod_eed = NULL, prod_haz = NULL) {

  tox_data_i  <- filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_base, L_tar_min)
  n_tox_i     <- nrow(tox_data_i)
  n_species_i <- dplyr::n_distinct(tox_data_i$Species)

  na_row <- function(note) {
    tibble::tibble(
      Matrix = matrix_label, L_tar_min = L_tar_min,
      CF_p50 = NA_real_, EED_q50 = NA_real_,
      n_tox_records = n_tox_i, n_species = n_species_i, HC5_median = NA_real_,
      RQ_p50_1D = NA_real_, RQ_p025_1D = NA_real_, RQ_p975_1D = NA_real_, P_exceed_1D = NA_real_,
      RQ_p50_MC2D = NA_real_, P_exceed_MC2D = NA_real_,
      CF_RSD_pct = NA_real_, RQ_p50_RSD_pct = NA_real_, note = note
    )
  }

  if (isTRUE(L_tar_min == 1) && !is.null(prod_cf)) {
    combined_cf_i <- prod_cf
    eed_boot_i    <- prod_eed
    haz_i         <- prod_haz
  } else {
    set.seed(seed_base)
    corr_i <- correct_and_bootstrap_eed(
      monitoring = monitoring_df, conc_col = "C_measured_pL", cpsd_fit = cpsd_fit,
      alpha_draws = alpha_draws, L_tar_min = L_tar_min, L_tar_max = 5000,
      n_draws = 3000, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95), slope_convention = "differential"
    )
    combined_cf_i <- corr_i$combined_cf
    eed_boot_i    <- corr_i$eed_boot

    set.seed(seed_base + 1)
    # matrix_function_safe() (R/mp_risk_utils.R): a local patched copy of
    # PSSDplusplus::matrix_function() -- the installed package's oversample-
    # then-slice logic for upper.tissue.trans.size.um silently under-fills
    # when x1M_set narrows the acceptance window (confirmed failing at
    # x1M_set >= 20 with this analysis's real river parameters); the patch
    # replaces only that block with a draw-until-quota-met loop using the
    # identical rnorm() parameters and filter conditions. See the function's
    # own roxygen comment for the full diagnosis. Installed PSSDplusplus is
    # never modified.
    param_matrix_i <- do.call(
      matrix_function_safe,
      c(list(n_sobol = n_boot, params = param_values_base, upper.tissue.truncation.limit = 500,
             x1M_set = L_tar_min, x2D_set = 5000), matrix_extra_args)
    ) |> rave_override_fn()

    # A high L_tar_min can leave too few (or zero) Food-Dilution-alignable
    # records after PSSDplusplus's own ingestible/size-gating logic runs
    # inside MC_sim_align_parallel(), even when the raw filtered tox_data_i
    # row count looks adequate -- build_haz_df() then has nothing to
    # summarise for that ERM. Caught here rather than crashing the render,
    # per the spec's own guardrail: flag as indicative-only (NA row with a
    # note) rather than treat as a production result.
    pssd_haz <- tryCatch({
      pssd_i <- run_pssd_pipeline(
        tox_data = tox_data_i, param_matrix = param_matrix_i, environments = environments,
        cache_suffix = paste0("m12_", matrix_label, "_", L_tar_min),
        dose_unit = "L", n_sim = n_boot, num_cores = parallel::detectCores() - 2,
        sim = 30, cv_uf = 0.5, rmore_method = "lognormal",
        seed = seed_base + 2, x1D_set = L_tar_min
      )
      haz_try <- build_haz_df(pssd_i$pSSDs, environments[1])
      if (is.null(haz_try) || nrow(haz_try) == 0 ||
          !any(haz_try$ERM == "Food Dilution" & haz_try$HCx == 5)) {
        list(ok = FALSE, note = "pSSD fit returned no Food Dilution HC5 at this floor")
      } else {
        list(ok = TRUE, haz = haz_try)
      }
    }, error = function(e) {
      list(ok = FALSE, note = paste0("pSSD/hazard fit failed: ", conditionMessage(e)))
    })

    if (!pssd_haz$ok) {
      return(na_row(pssd_haz$note))
    }
    haz_i <- pssd_haz$haz
  }

  set.seed(seed_base + 3)
  risk_draws_1d <- draw_rq_mc1d(haz_i, eed_boot_i$q50, n_risk = 1000)
  rs_1d <- summarize_rq(risk_draws_1d) |> dplyr::filter(ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5)
  rs_1d_ci <- risk_draws_1d |> dplyr::filter(ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5) |>
    dplyr::summarise(RQ_p025 = stats::quantile(RQ, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                      RQ_p975 = stats::quantile(RQ, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))

  mc2d_i <- mc2d_risk(monitoring_df = monitoring_df, combined_cf = combined_cf_i, haz_df = haz_i,
                       n_uncertainty = 100, n_variability = 500, seed = seed_base + 4)
  mc2d_food_hc5_i <- mc2d_i |> dplyr::filter(ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5)
  rs_mc2d <- mc2d_food_hc5_i |>
    dplyr::summarise(P_exceed_med = median(P_exceed), RQ_p50_med = median(RQ_p50))

  hc5_i <- haz_i |> dplyr::filter(ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5) |> dplyr::pull(PNEC) |> stats::median()

  # Uncertainty (not variability) at this floor: %RSD of the exposure-side CF
  # draws (correction_factor() output, one value per alpha_draws realization)
  # and %RSD of the outer-loop (uncertainty) RQ_p50 across mc2d_risk()'s
  # n_uncertainty = 100 CF+PNEC draws. Both are dispersion-of-the-estimate
  # measures, not the exposure variability captured by the inner loop --
  # answers "how much does our estimate of the risk move if we re-ran the
  # uncertain inputs," at each L_tar_min.
  cf_rsd_pct     <- 100 * stats::sd(combined_cf_i) / mean(combined_cf_i)
  rq_p50_rsd_pct <- 100 * stats::sd(mc2d_food_hc5_i$RQ_p50) / mean(mc2d_food_hc5_i$RQ_p50)

  tibble::tibble(
    Matrix = matrix_label, L_tar_min = L_tar_min,
    CF_p50 = stats::median(combined_cf_i), EED_q50 = stats::median(eed_boot_i$q50),
    n_tox_records = n_tox_i, n_species = n_species_i, HC5_median = hc5_i,
    RQ_p50_1D = rs_1d$RQ_p50, RQ_p025_1D = rs_1d_ci$RQ_p025, RQ_p975_1D = rs_1d_ci$RQ_p975, P_exceed_1D = rs_1d$P_exceed,
    RQ_p50_MC2D = rs_mc2d$RQ_p50_med, P_exceed_MC2D = rs_mc2d$P_exceed_med,
    CF_RSD_pct = cf_rsd_pct, RQ_p50_RSD_pct = rq_p50_rsd_pct, note = NA_character_
  )
}

rave_override_river <- function(pm) {
  pm |> dplyr::mutate(
    R.ave.water.freshwater = sample(R.ave_vals, size = dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE),
    H_W_ratio.freshwater   = sample(R.ave_vals, size = dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE)
  )
}
rave_override_ocean <- function(pm) {
  pm |> dplyr::mutate(
    R.ave.water.marine     = sample(R.ave_ocean_vals, size = dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE),
    H_W_ratio.water.marine = sample(R.ave_ocean_vals, size = dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE)
  )
}

m12_river_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(m12_floors, function(L) {
  m12_run_one_floor(
    L_tar_min = L, matrix_label = "River water", monitoring_df = monitoring,
    cpsd_fit = cpsd_fit_all, alpha_draws = alpha, tox_data_base = tox_data,
    param_values_base = param_values, environments = c("Freshwater"),
    matrix_extra_args = list(), rave_override_fn = rave_override_river,
    seed_base = 61000 + round(L * 10), prod_cf = combined_cf, prod_eed = eed_boot, prod_haz = haz
  )
}))

m12_ocean_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(m12_floors, function(L) {
  m12_run_one_floor(
    L_tar_min = L, matrix_label = "Ocean water", monitoring_df = monitoring_ocean,
    cpsd_fit = cpsd_fit_ocean_all, alpha_draws = alpha_ocean, tox_data_base = tox_data_ocean,
    param_values_base = param_values_ocean, environments = c("Marine"),
    matrix_extra_args = list(include_marine_surface_water = TRUE, include_freshwater_surface_water = FALSE,
                              include_marine_sediment = FALSE, include_freshwater_sediment = FALSE),
    rave_override_fn = rave_override_ocean,
    seed_base = 62000 + round(L * 10), prod_cf = combined_cf_ocean, prod_eed = eed_boot_ocean, prod_haz = haz_ocean
  )
}))
```

**Guardrails and interpretation.** The `L_tar_min = 1` µm row is the production headline and is unchanged by this analysis (reused, not recomputed). Any floor where `n_species` falls below the pSSD++ practical minimum is indicative only — read `n_species` in the table above before interpreting that row's RQ. If the Food Dilution median RQ and P(RQ>1) stay well above 1 across all four floors, the sub-floor extrapolation is not driving the exceedance conclusion (expected, since Food Dilution's volume-weighted dose model damps the sub-floor particle-*number* explosion); if the exceedance instead collapses at a higher floor, the conclusion is sensitive to the 1 µm extrapolation and that dependency should be stated plainly rather than averaged away.

### 12.5.1.1 Does restricting the analysis to sizes closer to the measured range reduce uncertainty?

`L_tar_min = 1` µm is the largest extrapolation below the measured detection window (`r round(cpsd_fit_all$lower_lod_used_um)`–`r round(cpsd_fit_all$upper_lod_um)` µm river, `r round(cpsd_fit_ocean_all$lower_lod_used_um)`–`r round(cpsd_fit_ocean_all$upper_lod_um)` µm ocean); raising the floor shortens that extrapolation. Two dispersion metrics separate this from the *magnitude* sensitivity shown above: (1) `CF_RSD_pct`, the relative standard deviation (%RSD = 100 x SD / mean) of the correction-factor draws themselves (`combined_cf_i`, one value per `alpha_draws` realization) -- a pure exposure-side uncertainty measure; and (2) `RQ_p50_RSD_pct`, the %RSD of the median RQ across `mc2d_risk()`'s `n_uncertainty` = 100 outer-loop draws (each redrawing one CF and one PNEC) -- i.e., how much our *estimate* of the median RQ itself moves if the uncertain inputs were redrawn, isolated from the inner-loop exposure *variability* that `RQ_p50_MC2D` above already integrates over.

```{r m12-uncertainty-vs-floor, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
m12_rsd_table <- m12_results |>
  dplyr::select(Matrix, L_tar_min, CF_RSD_pct, RQ_p50_RSD_pct, n_species, note)

knitr::kable(
  m12_rsd_table, digits = 1,
  caption = paste0(
    "Exposure (CF) and risk-estimate (RQ p50, MC2D outer/uncertainty loop) %RSD by extrapolation floor. ",
    "Lower %RSD = less relative dispersion in the estimate. NA rows are the same data-insufficient floors flagged above."
  ),
  col.names = c("Matrix", "L_tar_min (µm)", "CF %RSD", "RQ p50 %RSD", "n species", "Note")
)
```

**Interpretation.** For river water, CF %RSD moves from `r round(m12_rsd_river$CF_RSD_pct[1], 1)`% at `L_tar_min` = `r m12_rsd_river$L_tar_min[1]` µm to `r round(m12_rsd_river$CF_RSD_pct[nrow(m12_rsd_river)], 1)`% at `r m12_rsd_river$L_tar_min[nrow(m12_rsd_river)]` µm, and RQ p50 %RSD moves from `r round(m12_rsd_river$RQ_p50_RSD_pct[1], 1)`% to `r round(m12_rsd_river$RQ_p50_RSD_pct[nrow(m12_rsd_river)], 1)`% over the same range. For ocean water (valid floors only, `r paste(m12_rsd_ocean$L_tar_min, collapse=", ")` µm), CF %RSD moves from `r round(m12_rsd_ocean$CF_RSD_pct[1], 1)`% to `r round(m12_rsd_ocean$CF_RSD_pct[nrow(m12_rsd_ocean)], 1)`%, and RQ p50 %RSD from `r round(m12_rsd_ocean$RQ_p50_RSD_pct[1], 1)`% to `r round(m12_rsd_ocean$RQ_p50_RSD_pct[nrow(m12_rsd_ocean)], 1)`%. `r if (m12_rsd_river$CF_RSD_pct[nrow(m12_rsd_river)] < m12_rsd_river$CF_RSD_pct[1]) "Restricting the correction factor to sizes closer to the measured window does reduce exposure-side dispersion for river water, consistent with a shorter power-law extrapolation carrying less compounded uncertainty." else "Exposure-side dispersion does not monotonically shrink for river water as the floor is raised, so a shorter extrapolation window is not, by itself, guaranteed to reduce CF uncertainty here -- the alpha draw distribution and its interaction with the floor matter more than extrapolation length alone."` This is a **CF/RQ-estimate dispersion** result, not a data-availability result: it does not by itself justify raising the production floor above `L_tar_min` = 1 µm, because (a) the RQ *magnitude* sensitivity above already shows Food Dilution risk is not being driven by the sub-floor extrapolation, and (b) a higher floor discards real tox and monitoring size range along with the extrapolation, at the species-count cost quantified in Section 12.5.1.2 below and in the `n_species` column here.

### 12.5.1.2 Why does the ocean Food Dilution fit fail above L_tar_min = 10 µm?

```{r m12-ocean-floor-diagnostic, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Why ocean, not river, loses its Food Dilution fit above L_tar_min = 1 um --
# diagnostic only (not part of the m12_results pipeline above). Answers: is
# this a code bug, or a real property of the marine ToMEx subset? Computed
# from the same tox_data / tox_data_ocean / filter_tox_by_size_floor() the
# m12 pipeline itself uses, so the numbers below stay live.
m12_char_size <- function(d) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    d$polydispersity == "polydisperse" & !is.na(d$size.length.max.um.used.for.conversions) ~
      d$size.length.max.um.used.for.conversions,
    d$polydispersity == "monodisperse" & !is.na(d$size.length.um.used.for.conversions) ~
      d$size.length.um.used.for.conversions,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )
}

m12_diag <- list(
  river_sp1   = dplyr::n_distinct(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data, 1)$Species),
  river_sp20  = dplyr::n_distinct(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data, 20)$Species),
  ocean_sp1   = dplyr::n_distinct(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_ocean, 1)$Species),
  ocean_sp20  = dplyr::n_distinct(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_ocean, 20)$Species),
  ocean_fish1  = sum(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_ocean, 1)$Group  == "Fish"),
  ocean_fish20 = sum(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_ocean, 20)$Group == "Fish"),
  river_med_size = stats::median(m12_char_size(tox_data), na.rm = TRUE),
  ocean_med_size = stats::median(m12_char_size(tox_data_ocean), na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

Ocean's larger raw species pool is real (`r dplyr::n_distinct(tox_data_ocean$Species)` marine vs `r dplyr::n_distinct(tox_data$Species)` freshwater species pass the same QC filters before any size floor is applied) but it is concentrated at much smaller tested particle sizes: the marine subset's median characteristic tested size is `r round(m12_diag$ocean_med_size, 1)` µm against `r round(m12_diag$river_med_size, 1)` µm for freshwater, and `r round(100 * mean(tox_data_ocean$polydispersity == "monodisperse"), 0)`% of marine records are monodisperse (small, uniform test beads) versus `r round(100 * mean(tox_data$polydispersity == "monodisperse"), 0)`% for freshwater. Raising the floor to 20 µm therefore removes marine records disproportionately: usable species fall from `r m12_diag$ocean_sp1` to `r m12_diag$ocean_sp20` for ocean (a `r scales::percent(1 - m12_diag$ocean_sp20/m12_diag$ocean_sp1, accuracy = 1)` drop) versus `r m12_diag$river_sp1` to `r m12_diag$river_sp20` for river (`r scales::percent(1 - m12_diag$river_sp20/m12_diag$river_sp1, accuracy = 1)`). Fish records, the single largest marine Food-Dilution-relevant group at 1 µm, collapse from `r m12_diag$ocean_fish1` to `r m12_diag$ocean_fish20` -- almost all marine fish-feeding studies in this ToMEx subset used particles smaller than 20 µm. Once `run_pssd_pipeline()`'s own ingestibility/dose-positive/non-Algae gating runs on top of that, too few marine species remain for `PSSDplusplus` to construct a Food Dilution SSD at all at `L_tar_min` = 20 µm, so `pSSDs[["Tier3_Marine_Food Dilution"]]` is `NULL` and the row is flagged NA rather than fabricated -- this is a genuine data-sparsity limit of the current marine ToMEx subset at larger size floors, not a pipeline defect. The two finer intermediate floors (5, 10 µm) added below still resolve, confirming the failure is specific to the 20 µm floor rather than a broad breakdown of the marine pipeline.

## 12.5.2 Model-selection robustness: MLE and a tapered/lognormal small-end model

Distinct from Section 4.1's method-choice statement: this section does not ask whether C-PSD is the right method (it is; Segur et al. 2026 already established C-PSD ≈ MLE in accuracy). It asks how much the *risk result* depends on the sub-floor extrapolation model, given Segur et al.'s own caveat that C-PSD extrapolates below the measured range, and marine-surface literature suggesting the true small-end particle-size distribution may roll off (fewer small particles than a single power law implies) rather than continue as one power law to 1 µm.

Three models are fit to each matrix's pooled ("all" shapes) particle-length data: (a) the production C-PSD OLS fit (carried through for comparison, not refit here); (b) an MLE power law (`poweRlaw::conpl`), with `xmin` chosen by minimizing the Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic and a goodness-of-fit bootstrap p-value ([Clauset, Shalizi & Newman 2009](https://doi.org/10.1137/070710111); power law rejected if p < 0.1); and (c) a lognormal small-end alternative (`poweRlaw::conlnorm`) fit at the *same* `xmin` as the MLE power law, compared to it via a Vuong likelihood-ratio test (`compare_distributions()`). Ocean fiber (5 populated C-PSD bins; Section 12.1.1) is excluded from MLE fitting as too sparse for a stable tail fit.

```{r m13-model-fits, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
m13_fit_one_matrix <- function(length_vec, matrix_label, seed) {
  length_vec <- length_vec[is.finite(length_vec) & length_vec > 0]

  m_pl <- poweRlaw::conpl$new(length_vec)
  est  <- poweRlaw::estimate_xmin(m_pl)
  m_pl$setXmin(est)

  set.seed(seed)
  bp <- poweRlaw::bootstrap_p(m_pl, no_of_sims = 100, threads = 1, seed = seed)

  m_ln <- poweRlaw::conlnorm$new(length_vec)
  m_ln$setXmin(m_pl$getXmin())
  m_ln$setPars(poweRlaw::estimate_pars(m_ln))

  comp <- poweRlaw::compare_distributions(m_pl, m_ln)

  list(
    matrix_label = matrix_label,
    n_total = length(length_vec),
    xmin = est$xmin, ntail = est$ntail, alpha_mle = m_pl$pars,
    KS_D = est$gof, bootstrap_p = bp$p,
    meanlog = m_ln$pars[1], sdlog = m_ln$pars[2],
    vuong_stat = comp$test_statistic, vuong_p = comp$p_two_sided
  )
}

m13_river_fit <- m13_fit_one_matrix(raw_particles_river$length_um, "River water", seed = 71001)
m13_ocean_fit <- m13_fit_one_matrix(raw_particles_ocean$length_um, "Ocean water", seed = 71002)

m13_fit_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list(m13_river_fit, m13_ocean_fit), function(f) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Matrix = f$matrix_label, n_total = f$n_total, xmin_um = round(f$xmin, 1), n_tail = f$ntail,
    alpha_MLE = round(f$alpha_mle, 3), KS_D = round(f$KS_D, 4), bootstrap_p = round(f$bootstrap_p, 3),
    power_law_rejected = f$bootstrap_p < 0.1,
    vuong_stat = round(f$vuong_stat, 3), vuong_p = round(f$vuong_p, 3),
    lognormal_meanlog = round(f$meanlog, 3), lognormal_sdlog = round(f$sdlog, 3)
  )
}))

knitr::kable(
  m13_fit_summary,
  caption = "M1.3: MLE power-law fit (poweRlaw::conpl) and lognormal comparator (poweRlaw::conlnorm) at the same xmin, river and ocean pooled particle-length PSDs"
)
```

```{r m13-rq-propagation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Convert each model to an equivalent correction factor over the SAME measured
# window already used for the production C-PSD correction factor
# (L_meas_min_use/L_meas_max_use), so only the extrapolation MODEL differs,
# not the physical measurement window -- then recompute the RQ for both ERMs
# against the already-computed production hazard (haz/haz_ocean; hazard is
# not re-derived here, only the exposure-side extrapolation model changes).
m13_propagate_one <- function(fit, L_meas_min, L_meas_max, monitoring_df, conc_col,
                               haz_df, n_risk, cpsd_a_psd, combined_cf_prod, seed_base) {

  cf_mle <- correction_factor(
    a = -fit$alpha_mle, L_meas_min = L_meas_min, L_meas_max = L_meas_max,
    L_tar_min = 1, L_tar_max = 5000, slope_convention = "differential"
  )
  cf_lognormal <- (stats::plnorm(5000, fit$meanlog, fit$sdlog) - stats::plnorm(1, fit$meanlog, fit$sdlog)) /
    (stats::plnorm(L_meas_max, fit$meanlog, fit$sdlog) - stats::plnorm(L_meas_min, fit$meanlog, fit$sdlog))

  rq_for_cf <- function(cf_val, seed) {
    set.seed(seed)
    eed_i <- bootstrap_eed(monitoring_df[[conc_col]] * cf_val, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95))
    set.seed(seed + 1)
    summarize_rq(draw_rq_mc1d(haz_df, eed_i$q50, n_risk = n_risk)) |>
      dplyr::filter(ERM %in% c("Food Dilution", "Tissue Translocation"), HCx == 5) |>
      dplyr::select(ERM, RQ_p50, P_exceed)
  }

  dplyr::bind_rows(
    rq_for_cf(median(combined_cf_prod), seed_base)     |> dplyr::mutate(Model = "C-PSD (production)", CF = median(combined_cf_prod)),
    rq_for_cf(cf_mle, seed_base + 10)                   |> dplyr::mutate(Model = "MLE power law", CF = cf_mle),
    rq_for_cf(cf_lognormal, seed_base + 20)              |> dplyr::mutate(Model = "Lognormal (tapered small-end)", CF = cf_lognormal)
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(Matrix = fit$matrix_label)
}

m13_river_rq <- m13_propagate_one(
  m13_river_fit, L_meas_min_use, L_meas_max_use, monitoring, "C_measured_pL",
  haz, n_risk, cpsd_fit_all$a_psd, combined_cf, seed_base = 72001
)
m13_ocean_rq <- m13_propagate_one(
  m13_ocean_fit, L_meas_min_ocean, L_meas_max_ocean, monitoring_ocean, "C_measured_pL",
  haz_ocean, n_risk_ocean, cpsd_fit_ocean_all$a_psd, combined_cf_ocean, seed_base = 72002
)

m13_rq_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(m13_river_rq, m13_ocean_rq) |>
  dplyr::relocate(Matrix, Model, ERM, CF, RQ_p50, P_exceed)

knitr::kable(
  m13_rq_results, digits = 3,
  caption = "M1.3: Food Dilution and Tissue Translocation HC5 RQ under each extrapolation model, holding hazard fixed at the production values"
)
```

```{r m13-rq-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
m13_rq_plot <- m13_rq_results |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = Model, y = RQ_p50, color = ERM, shape = Matrix)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3.5, position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = ERM_PALETTE, name = "ERM") +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL, y = "HC5 median RQ [log10 scale]",
    title = "RQ under each extrapolation model: C-PSD vs. MLE power law vs. lognormal small-end",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = RQ = 1. Hazard held at production values; only the exposure-side extrapolation model varies."
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4))

ggsave(m13_rq_plot, filename = "figures/m13_rq_plot.png", width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300)
m13_rq_plot
```

**Guardrails and interpretation.** The C-PSD single-slope fit remains the production default; MLE and lognormal are labeled comparators only, and hazard is never re-derived in this section (only the exposure-side extrapolation model changes, holding `haz`/`haz_ocean` fixed at their production values). Report GoF failures honestly: `r if (m13_fit_summary$power_law_rejected[m13_fit_summary$Matrix == "River water"]) "the power law IS rejected for river water (bootstrap p < 0.1)" else "the power law is NOT rejected for river water"`, and `r if (m13_fit_summary$power_law_rejected[m13_fit_summary$Matrix == "Ocean water"]) "IS rejected for ocean water" else "is NOT rejected for ocean water"` (bootstrap p = `r round(m13_fit_summary$bootstrap_p[m13_fit_summary$Matrix=="River water"],3)` river, `r round(m13_fit_summary$bootstrap_p[m13_fit_summary$Matrix=="Ocean water"],3)` ocean). The Vuong test indicates whether the power law and lognormal are statistically distinguishable at each matrix's shared `xmin` (p < 0.05 favors one model over the other; a non-significant result means the data cannot discriminate between them at this sample size). If the Food Dilution exceedance conclusion holds across all three models, the risk result is robust to the extrapolation-model choice; if it flips under the lognormal small-end model, that sensitivity should be stated plainly.

## 12.5.3 River vs ocean polymer composition: test for buoyant-polymer enrichment

A shift in polymer mix at the sea surface — specifically enrichment of buoyant polymers (PP, PE) relative to rivers — would independently support a surface-retention/transport interpretation of the shallower ocean particle-length PSD slope (Section 12.1.1), rather than a source/residence or fitting-window explanation. `buoyancy_freshwater`/`buoyancy_marine` are already assigned per particle by `assign_polymer_density()` (Section 3.1.1), relative to freshwater (1.00 g/cm³) and seawater (1.025 g/cm³) respectively, so no new density-assignment code is needed here — only the statistical test.

```{r m14-polymer-composition, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# sample_depth_general is entirely NA for every ocean-water particle in this
# study (all 6 ocean sample IDs; confirmed below) -- these µFTIR runs simply
# did not record a depth stratum for ocean grabs, unlike river water, which
# has both strata. Ocean is therefore its own "depth not recorded" level
# rather than being assumed to be "surface" -- no depth label is fabricated
# for data that was not collected with one.
m14_particles <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  raw_particles_river |> dplyr::mutate(Matrix = "River water"),
  raw_particles_ocean |> dplyr::mutate(Matrix = "Ocean water")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Depth = dplyr::case_when(
      Matrix == "Ocean water" ~ "depth not recorded",
      TRUE ~ as.character(sample_depth_general)
    )
  )

m14_ocean_depth_recorded <- sum(!is.na(raw_particles_ocean$sample_depth_general))

m14_contingency <- table(m14_particles$polymer_density_group, m14_particles$Matrix)

knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame.matrix(m14_contingency),
  caption = paste0(
    "River (n = ", sum(m14_particles$Matrix == "River water"), ") vs ocean (n = ",
    sum(m14_particles$Matrix == "Ocean water"), ") polymer-group contingency table."
  )
)

# Fisher's exact if any expected cell count is small (chi-square approximation
# becomes unreliable below ~5 expected per cell); chi-square otherwise.
m14_expected_min <- suppressWarnings(min(chisq.test(m14_contingency)$expected))
m14_full_test <- if (m14_expected_min < 5) {
  fisher.test(m14_contingency, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)
} else {
  chisq.test(m14_contingency)
}
cat(
  "Full polymer x matrix test:", m14_full_test$method,
  "-- statistic =", if (!is.null(m14_full_test$statistic)) signif(m14_full_test$statistic, 4) else NA,
  ", p =", signif(m14_full_test$p.value, 4),
  "(min expected cell count =", round(m14_expected_min, 2), ")\n"
)
```

```{r m14-buoyant-2x2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Focused 2x2 test: buoyant (PP + PE) vs non-buoyant, river vs ocean. PP and PE
# are the only two polymer groups classified "buoyant" under both
# buoyancy_freshwater and buoyancy_marine in this dataset (verified below),
# so "buoyant" here is defined directly by polymer identity rather than by
# picking one of the two medium-specific buoyancy columns.
m14_particles <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::mutate(is_buoyant = polymer_density_group %in% c("polyethylene", "polypropylene"))

m14_buoyancy_agreement <- mean(m14_particles$buoyancy_freshwater == m14_particles$buoyancy_marine)

m14_2x2 <- table(m14_particles$is_buoyant, m14_particles$Matrix)
m14_2x2_test <- if (min(suppressWarnings(chisq.test(m14_2x2)$expected)) < 5) {
  fisher.test(m14_2x2)
} else {
  chisq.test(m14_2x2, correct = TRUE)
}

m14_buoyant_fraction <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::group_by(Matrix) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    n_buoyant = sum(is_buoyant),
    fraction_buoyant = n_buoyant / n,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ci = list(stats::binom.test(n_buoyant, n)$conf.int),
    ci_low  = ci[1],
    ci_high = ci[2]
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(-ci)

knitr::kable(
  m14_buoyant_fraction, digits = 3,
  caption = "Buoyant-polymer (PP + PE) fraction by matrix, with binomial 95% CIs",
  col.names = c("Matrix", "n", "n buoyant", "Fraction buoyant", "95% CI low", "95% CI high")
)

cat(
  "Buoyant (PP+PE) vs non-buoyant x river/ocean:", m14_2x2_test$method,
  "-- p =", signif(m14_2x2_test$p.value, 4), "\n"
)
cat(
  "buoyancy_freshwater and buoyancy_marine agree for", scales::percent(m14_buoyancy_agreement, accuracy = 0.1),
  "of particles in this dataset -- i.e. essentially no polymer group in the current density lookup ",
  "(Hidalgo-Ruz et al. 2012) falls in the narrow density band (1.00-1.025 g/cm3) that would flip ",
  "classification between freshwater and seawater reference density.\n"
)
```

```{r m14-composition-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
m14_composition_plot <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::count(Matrix, polymer_density_group) |>
  dplyr::group_by(Matrix) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fraction = n / sum(n)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = polymer_density_group, y = fraction, fill = Matrix)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("River water" = "#0072B2", "Ocean water" = "#009E73"), name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Fraction of particles",
    title = "River vs ocean polymer composition",
    subtitle = "PP (polypropylene) and PE (polyethylene) are the buoyant classes tested in the 2x2 comparison below"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4))

ggsave(m14_composition_plot, filename = "figures/m14_composition_plot.png", width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300)
m14_composition_plot

m14_buoyant_plot <- m14_buoyant_fraction |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = Matrix, y = fraction_buoyant, color = Matrix)) +
  ggplot2::geom_pointrange(ggplot2::aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), size = 0.8, linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("River water" = "#0072B2", "Ocean water" = "#009E73"), guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Buoyant (PP + PE) fraction, with binomial 95% CI",
    title = "Buoyant-polymer fraction: river vs ocean"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4))

ggsave(m14_buoyant_plot, filename = "figures/m14_buoyant_plot.png", width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
m14_buoyant_plot
```

**Interpretation.** A significant enrichment of PP/PE in ocean surface water relative to river water (`r scales::percent(m14_buoyant_fraction$fraction_buoyant[m14_buoyant_fraction$Matrix == "Ocean water"], accuracy=0.1)` vs `r scales::percent(m14_buoyant_fraction$fraction_buoyant[m14_buoyant_fraction$Matrix == "River water"], accuracy=0.1)`, 2×2 test p = `r signif(m14_2x2_test$p.value, 3)`) would support the transport/retention reading of the river-vs-ocean slope difference; a null result points instead toward a source/residence or fitting-window explanation. **Caveats.** Composition is count-based over each matrix's own measured detection window (the same LOD/window caveats that apply to the slope fits themselves), and ocean n = `r sum(m14_particles$Matrix == "Ocean water")` limits statistical power relative to river n = `r sum(m14_particles$Matrix == "River water")`. This polymer-composition test is an independent line of evidence that does *not* depend on the fitting window — but the river-vs-ocean **slope** difference itself (Section 12.1.1) is separately confounded by different fitting windows (river `r round(cpsd_fit_all$lower_lod_used_um)`–`r round(cpsd_fit_all$upper_lod_um)` µm vs ocean `r round(cpsd_fit_ocean_all$lower_lod_used_um)`–`r round(cpsd_fit_ocean_all$upper_lod_um)` µm) and should be re-tested over a common overlapping window before that slope difference alone is attributed to source or transport.

### 12.5.3.1 Depth-stratified polymer composition (river surface/subsurface vs ocean)

River water has both `sample_depth_general` strata (`r sum(raw_particles_river$sample_depth_general == "surface", na.rm=TRUE)` surface, `r sum(raw_particles_river$sample_depth_general == "subsurface", na.rm=TRUE)` subsurface particles). Ocean water does not: `sample_depth_general` is unrecorded for all `r nrow(raw_particles_ocean)` ocean-water particles in this study (`r m14_ocean_depth_recorded` with a recorded stratum), so an ocean depth split is not possible from this dataset -- ocean is shown below as its own "depth not recorded" panel rather than assumed to be surface-only. The top-5 polymers by pooled river+ocean particle count set a common comparison basis across panels; every other polymer group is collapsed to "Other" so rare groups do not fragment the comparison.

```{r m14-depth-composition-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
m14_top5_polymers <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::count(polymer_density_group, sort = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 5) |>
  dplyr::pull(polymer_density_group)

m14_depth_panel_levels <- c("River water - surface", "River water - subsurface", "Ocean water - depth not recorded")

m14_depth_composition <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    polymer_top5 = ifelse(polymer_density_group %in% m14_top5_polymers,
                           as.character(polymer_density_group), "Other"),
    polymer_top5 = factor(polymer_top5, levels = c(m14_top5_polymers, "Other")),
    panel = factor(paste(Matrix, Depth, sep = " - "), levels = m14_depth_panel_levels)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(panel)) |>
  dplyr::count(panel, polymer_top5) |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fraction = n / sum(n), n_panel = sum(n)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

m14_depth_composition_plot <- m14_depth_composition |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = polymer_top5, y = fraction, fill = polymer_top5)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.2) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 3,
                       labeller = ggplot2::as_labeller(function(x) paste0(x, "\n(n = ",
                         m14_depth_composition$n_panel[match(x, m14_depth_composition$panel)], ")"))) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Fraction of particles",
    title = "Top-5 polymer composition by matrix and sampling depth",
    subtitle = "Ocean has no recorded depth stratum in this dataset (see text) -- shown as a single panel, not assumed to be surface"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
    panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggsave(m14_depth_composition_plot, filename = "figures/m14_depth_composition_plot.png", width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300)
m14_depth_composition_plot
```

**Interpretation.** Comparing the two river panels isolates a within-matrix depth effect (same sampling program, same µFTIR workflow, same LOD window); comparing either river panel to the ocean panel still mixes a matrix effect with the unrecorded-depth limitation above. `r scales::percent(m14_buoyant_fraction$fraction_buoyant[m14_buoyant_fraction$Matrix == "Ocean water"], accuracy=0.1)` buoyant fraction in ocean vs river's surface/subsurface split (Section 12.5.3 table) is the more decision-relevant comparison than the full multi-polymer breakdown shown here, which is provided as a descriptive, hypothesis-generating cross-tabulation rather than an additional formal test.
