## 15.1 Revised uncertainty interpretation

The main unresolved methodological uncertainties are now: (1) µFTIR objective and the marginal 50–100 µm detection zone, and (2) transport-induced PSD structural uncertainty described by Hoffman et al. (2026). The latter can affect absolute concentrations through the CF exponent, and may also affect relative comparisons when surface/subsurface samples, fibers/fragments, or buoyant/settling polymers are mixed in a pooled single-power-law fit. The sensitivity analyses above therefore replace the older conclusion that no further correction was warranted. The calibrated interpretation is that the Food Dilution pathway remains the dominant ERM in this screening assessment, while magnitude estimates should be read together with the slope-uncertainty, depth-stratified, density/buoyancy, and water-sediment coherence diagnostics.

## 15.2 Modeling priorities

Hoffman et al. (2026) indicates that 3-D particle geometry and density inputs should be improved before investing effort in more complex settling-velocity equations. The current report follows that guardrail by adding polymer-resolved density and buoyancy flags, making δ and K explicit assumptions in the critical-size calculation, and retaining settling-based diagnostics as bias-level sensitivity checks rather than high-precision corrections. Future transport work should prioritize measured particle thickness, density, and shape-specific behavior; settling-equation refinements alone should not be expected to remove the dominant uncertainty.

## 15.3 Revised executive summary

```{r spec3b-exec-summary-inline, include=FALSE}
fd_river_hc5 <- dplyr::filter(risk_summary,       ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5)
tt_river_hc5 <- dplyr::filter(risk_summary,       ERM == "Tissue Translocation", HCx == 5)
fd_sed_hc5   <- dplyr::filter(risk_summary_sed,   ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5)
tt_sed_hc5   <- dplyr::filter(risk_summary_sed,   ERM == "Tissue Translocation", HCx == 5)
fd_legacy_av_hc5 <- dplyr::filter(risk_summary_legacy_river, ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5)
fd_collapse_river <- fd_legacy_av_hc5$RQ_p50 / fd_river_hc5$RQ_p50
```

This section restates the executive summary with the corrected numbers now that every matrix's corrected and legacy sensitivity pipeline (Sections 5-14) has been computed, per SPEC 3b.

**(a) Corrected Food Dilution RQ, after SPEC 1b.** At `r if (is_production_budget) "the production" else "a dev-scale iteration"` Monte Carlo budget (`r n_boot` parameter-matrix replicates, `r n_mc` slope draws), the corrected median Food Dilution HC5 RQ is `r round(fd_river_hc5$RQ_p50, 3)` for river water (P(RQ>1) = `r round(fd_river_hc5$P_exceed*100,1)`%) and `r round(rs_ocean_food_hc5$RQ_p50_med, 3)` for ocean water (median P(RQ>1) = `r round(rs_ocean_food_hc5$P_exceed_med*100,1)`%). **Sediment is intentionally omitted from this headline figure (SPEC 1d):** its nominal corrected Food Dilution HC5 RQ (`r round(fd_sed_hc5$RQ_p50, 3)`, P(RQ>1) = `r round(fd_sed_hc5$P_exceed*100,1)`%) is not a defensible risk estimate — Section 11.3.0/11.4.0 trace this to a placeholder exposure concentration (a per-liter water value reused as particles/kg) and a derived HC5 that fails the benthic-plausibility guard by roughly eleven orders of magnitude — so it is excluded from the risk conclusion rather than reported alongside the river and ocean values.

**(b) The prior (SPEC 1b-uncorrected) Food Dilution RQ was inflated by the volume-slope convention error.** Reverting only `a.v`/`a.sa`/`a.m` to the legacy cumulative-as-differential convention (Appendix A), holding exposure and the length-slope alignment at their corrected values, the river-water Food Dilution HC5 median RQ becomes `r round(fd_legacy_av_hc5$RQ_p50, 3)` — a `r round(fd_collapse_river, 1)`-fold change relative to the corrected value of `r round(fd_river_hc5$RQ_p50, 3)`. This is the same mechanism and direction of error described in the SPEC 1b background (a mean-particle-volume sensitivity calculation there estimates a ~4-6 million-fold effect at a = 0.76 vs. 1.68); the exact factor is a function of `n_boot`/`n_mc` and is expected to scale toward that estimate as the budget increases. **No Food Dilution RQ figure in this report should be read as ~10^7** — that magnitude describes the pre-SPEC-1b (legacy) error being corrected here, not the corrected result.

**(c) Tissue Translocation shift after both the length-slope and surface-area-slope fixes (revised, SPEC 3c).** Reverting only the hazard-side length-slope alignment to its legacy cumulative-as-differential form, the river-water Tissue Translocation HC5 P(RQ>1) is `r round(tt_legacy$P_exceed*100,1)`%, versus `r round(tt_now$P_exceed*100,1)`% under the corrected alignment (Section 14.1). This is a material driver, but so is the surface-area slope: reverting `a.v`/`a.sa`/`a.m` together gives `r round(tt_legacy_av$P_exceed*100,1)`%, and isolating `a.sa` alone gives `r round(tt_legacy_asa$P_exceed*100,1)`% — both far from the `r round(tt_now$P_exceed*100,1)`% corrected value, because Tissue Translocation/oxidative-stress alignment is surface-area-weighted and therefore directly sensitive to the `a.sa` correction, unlike its (correctly) minimal sensitivity to the volume slope alone. A prior version of this narrative incorrectly called the volume/area effect on Tissue Translocation "essentially unchanged"; that claim is retracted here (Section 14.1 has the corrected attribution and the full one-at-a-time decomposition table, now covering both ERMs).

**(d) Exposure as a single-slope-vs-piecewise bounding range (SPEC 2b).** The production single-slope correction factor and its piecewise (dual-slope) bounding alternative are compared per matrix in Section 13.3 (Tables: single-slope vs. piecewise CF/EED, and the resulting Food Dilution/Tissue Translocation HC5 RQ range). The single-slope CF remains the production default; the piecewise result is a labeled sensitivity bound quantifying structural (model-form) uncertainty in the unconstrained 1 µm-to-LOD sub-window, per the guardrails in the corrective-revision spec.

**(e) Sediment pathway excluded from the headline conclusion (SPEC 1d).** The sediment (beach sand) risk characterization in Section 11 is retained in this report as a methods/illustrative demonstration only. Its exposure concentration is not a genuine particles/kg-dry-weight value (Section 11.3.0), its hazard-side dose_unit = "kg" pathway was traced and found unit-consistent on its own terms with no discrete conversion bug identified (Section 11.4.0), and its sediment-specific ERM alignment slopes were independently verified correct and ruled out as the cause (Section 11.2, SPEC 1d-iv). The resulting sediment Food Dilution HC5 fails a rendered plausibility guard anchored on Redondo-Hasselerharm et al. (2023) by roughly eleven orders of magnitude. Until a genuine dry-weight sediment concentration is available, no sediment RQ in this report should be treated as a risk finding.

**(f) Sediment as a time-dependent, accumulating compartment (SPEC 1e).** Independent of the exposure-concentration problem in (e), Section 11.5 reframes sediment as an accumulating depositional sink in which deposited microplastics continue to fragment in place, so both bioaccessible exposure and hazard (HC5, via which benthic species become size-accessible) evolve over residence time ([Thuy-Dung, Groenenberg & Koelmans 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s43591-026-00210-8)). Any static sediment metric — including the illustrative Section 11.4 figures — is therefore a **lower-bound snapshot**, not an equilibrium value. Section 11.5.2 demonstrates this illustratively with a labeled, non-quantitative PSD-shift sensitivity showing the derived Food Dilution and Tissue Translocation HC5 falling as the sediment PSD is shifted progressively finer; Section 11.5.4 adds a most-sensitive-species screen (sediment, plus a river/ocean companion) since individual-species risk can precede a derivable community SSD signal. This is a framework/sensitivity addition — it does not change point (e): sediment remains excluded from the headline risk conclusion.

**Summary.** Food Dilution remains the risk-dominant ERM relative to Tissue Translocation for river and ocean water in this screening assessment, consistent with the qualitative conclusion of the prior revision; the sediment pathway is excluded from this conclusion pending real concentration data (point (e) above). The magnitude of the Food Dilution RQ, however, depends materially on which of the three convention fixes above is applied, and the decomposition in Appendix A is intended to make that dependency auditable rather than implicit.

## 15.4 individual-species RCR — river/ocean companion screen

Section 11.5.4 added a most-sensitive-species screen for the sediment benthic dataset. This subsection completes SPEC 1e-iv's companion request for the water compartments where exposure *is* quantitative (river, ocean): the single most sensitive species per ERM, plus the individual-species risk characterization ratio RCR = EED / lowest-species EC, reported as an early-warning companion to the community-HC5 RQ already characterized in Sections 7/12. This is placed here, after Section 15.3, because it is the first point in document execution order at which every matrix's hazard (`haz`/`haz_ocean`) and EED (`eed_boot`/`eed_boot_ocean`) objects all exist together.

```{r spec1e-iv-river-ocean-mss}
mss_river <- most_sensitive_species(erm_registry,       dose_col = "dose_new_particles_L")
mss_ocean <- most_sensitive_species(erm_registry_ocean, dose_col = "dose_new_particles_L")

mss_all_matrices <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(mss_river, Matrix = "River water",  .before = 1),
  dplyr::mutate(mss_ocean, Matrix = "Ocean water",  .before = 1),
  dplyr::mutate(mss_sed,   Matrix = "Sediment",     .before = 1)
)

knitr::kable(
  mss_all_matrices,
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste0(
    "SPEC 1e-iv: most-sensitive-species screen across all three matrices. median_EC is particles/L (river, ocean) ",
    "or particles/kg dw (sediment). Sediment rows are non-quantitative (SPEC 1d) and repeated here only for a ",
    "single cross-matrix reference table; see Section 11.5.4 for the sediment-specific interpretation."
  )
)
```

```{r spec1e-iv-river-ocean-rcr}
mss_river_fd <- dplyr::filter(mss_river, ERM == "Food Dilution")
mss_river_tt <- dplyr::filter(mss_river, ERM == "Tissue Translocation")
mss_ocean_fd <- dplyr::filter(mss_ocean, ERM == "Food Dilution")
mss_ocean_tt <- dplyr::filter(mss_ocean, ERM == "Tissue Translocation")

rcr_river_fd <- individual_species_rcr(eed_boot$q50,       mss_river_fd$median_EC)
rcr_river_tt <- individual_species_rcr(eed_boot$q50,       mss_river_tt$median_EC)
rcr_ocean_fd <- individual_species_rcr(eed_boot_ocean$q50, mss_ocean_fd$median_EC)
rcr_ocean_tt <- individual_species_rcr(eed_boot_ocean$q50, mss_ocean_tt$median_EC)

rs_river_fd_hc5 <- dplyr::filter(risk_summary,       ERM == "Food Dilution",        HCx == 5)
rs_river_tt_hc5 <- dplyr::filter(risk_summary,       ERM == "Tissue Translocation", HCx == 5)
rs_ocean_fd_hc5 <- dplyr::filter(risk_summary_ocean, ERM == "Food Dilution",        HCx == 5)
rs_ocean_tt_hc5 <- dplyr::filter(risk_summary_ocean, ERM == "Tissue Translocation", HCx == 5)

individual_species_rcr_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  Matrix                 = c("River water", "River water", "Ocean water", "Ocean water"),
  ERM                    = c("Food Dilution", "Tissue Translocation", "Food Dilution", "Tissue Translocation"),
  Most_sensitive_species = c(mss_river_fd$Species, mss_river_tt$Species, mss_ocean_fd$Species, mss_ocean_tt$Species),
  Individual_RCR_p50     = c(rcr_river_fd$RCR_p50, rcr_river_tt$RCR_p50, rcr_ocean_fd$RCR_p50, rcr_ocean_tt$RCR_p50),
  Individual_P_exceed    = c(rcr_river_fd$P_exceed, rcr_river_tt$P_exceed, rcr_ocean_fd$P_exceed, rcr_ocean_tt$P_exceed),
  Community_HC5_RQ_p50   = c(rs_river_fd_hc5$RQ_p50, rs_river_tt_hc5$RQ_p50, rs_ocean_fd_hc5$RQ_p50, rs_ocean_tt_hc5$RQ_p50),
  Community_P_exceed     = c(rs_river_fd_hc5$P_exceed, rs_river_tt_hc5$P_exceed, rs_ocean_fd_hc5$P_exceed, rs_ocean_tt_hc5$P_exceed)
)

knitr::kable(
  individual_species_rcr_tbl,
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste0(
    "Individual-species RCR (EED / lowest-species EC) vs. the community-HC5 RQ, river and ocean water. ",
    "Both share the same P(exceed) definition (fraction of bootstrap draws with ratio > 1)."
  )
)
```

Per Thuy-Dung et al. (2026), an individual-species RCR>1 can precede a derivable community-HC5 RQ signal by roughly a decade — the table above is therefore read as an early-warning companion, not a substitute for the community-HC5 RQ already reported in Sections 7 and 12. **This companion screen does not change any headline conclusion**: it reuses the same production `haz`/`eed_boot` objects without modification, and is additive/diagnostic only.

# Appendices

The three appendices below hold convention-validation history, implementation-validation detail, and exploratory/non-quantitative sediment material that support the results above but are not needed to read them. Every number in this document -- including here -- is produced by the same live code as the main body; nothing here is retyped. SPEC-numbered labels below are preserved from `docs/CHANGELOG_hoffman_revisions.md`, which is the authoritative provenance record for each revision.

## Appendix A: Convention-validation history

The differential-slope convention (length, area, volume, mass; Sections 5, 7) is the current basis throughout this report. This appendix quantifies the effect of each prior convention error that the SPEC 1/1b/3b/3c revisions corrected, and is why no number in the report body should be read as the pre-fix (≈10⁷, Food Dilution) legacy magnitude.

## A.1 all-matrix CF before/after (legacy cumulative vs. corrected differential)

Reruns the correction-factor convention check of Section 5.1 for all three matrices at once, comparing the legacy (cumulative slope passed as differential), corrected fit-only, and corrected structural-SD CF distributions side by side.

```{r hoffman-cf-before-after-all}
cf_case_summary <- function(matrix_label, cpsd_fit, combined_cf_current,
                            Lmin_use, Lmax_use, current_slope_draws, n = n_mc) {
  set.seed(4000 + nchar(matrix_label))
  cumulative_draws <- alpha_dist(mu = cpsd_fit$a_cpsd, sd = cpsd_fit$se_a_cpsd, n = n, structural_sd = 0)
  differential_fit_draws <- alpha_dist(mu = cpsd_fit$a_psd, sd = cpsd_fit$se_a_psd, n = n, structural_sd = 0)
  legacy_cf <- correction_factor(
    a = cumulative_draws,
    L_meas_min = Lmin_use,
    L_meas_max = Lmax_use,
    L_tar_min = 1,
    L_tar_max = 5000,
    slope_convention = "differential"
  )
  corrected_fit_cf <- correction_factor(
    a = differential_fit_draws,
    L_meas_min = Lmin_use,
    L_meas_max = Lmax_use,
    L_tar_min = 1,
    L_tar_max = 5000,
    slope_convention = "differential"
  )
  tibble::tibble(
    Matrix = matrix_label,
    Case = c("Legacy cumulative slope passed as differential", "Corrected differential slope, fit SE only", "Corrected differential slope plus structural SD"),
    Slope_p50 = c(median(cumulative_draws), median(differential_fit_draws), median(current_slope_draws)),
    CF_p05 = c(quantile(legacy_cf, 0.05), quantile(corrected_fit_cf, 0.05), quantile(combined_cf_current, 0.05)),
    CF_p50 = c(median(legacy_cf), median(corrected_fit_cf), median(combined_cf_current)),
    CF_p95 = c(quantile(legacy_cf, 0.95), quantile(corrected_fit_cf, 0.95), quantile(combined_cf_current, 0.95))
  )
}

cf_before_after_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cf_case_summary("River water", cpsd_fit_all, combined_cf, L_meas_min_use, L_meas_max_use, alpha),
  cf_case_summary("Sediment", cpsd_fit_sed_all, combined_cf_sed, L_meas_min_use_sed, L_meas_max_use_sed, alpha_sed),
  cf_case_summary("Ocean water", cpsd_fit_ocean_all, combined_cf_ocean, L_meas_min_ocean, L_meas_max_ocean, alpha_ocean)
)

knitr::kable(
  cf_before_after_all,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "SPEC 1 all-matrix CF before/after: cumulative-vs-differential slope convention"
)
```

River-only version of the same check (Section 5.1), computed here so `legacy_cf_river` is available for the SPEC 3b decomposition below (A.3):

```{r spec1-river-cf-before-after}
set.seed(9201)
legacy_cf_river <- correction_factor(
  a = alpha_dist(mu = cpsd_fit_all$a_cpsd, sd = cpsd_fit_all$se_a_cpsd, n = n_mc, structural_sd = 0),
  L_meas_min = L_meas_min_use,
  L_meas_max = L_meas_max_use,
  L_tar_min = 1,
  L_tar_max = 5000,
  slope_convention = "differential"
)
fit_only_cf_river <- correction_factor(
  a = alpha_fit_only,
  L_meas_min = L_meas_min_use,
  L_meas_max = L_meas_max_use,
  L_tar_min = 1,
  L_tar_max = 5000,
  slope_convention = "differential"
)
cf_before_after_river <- tibble::tibble(
  Matrix = "River water",
  Case = c("Legacy cumulative slope passed as differential", "Corrected differential slope, fit SE only", "Corrected differential slope plus structural SD"),
  slope_median = c(median(legacy_cf_river * 0 + alpha_dist(mu = cpsd_fit_all$a_cpsd, sd = cpsd_fit_all$se_a_cpsd, n = n_mc, structural_sd = 0)),
                   median(alpha_fit_only),
                   median(alpha)),
  CF_p05 = c(quantile(legacy_cf_river, 0.05), quantile(fit_only_cf_river, 0.05), quantile(combined_cf, 0.05)),
  CF_p50 = c(median(legacy_cf_river), median(fit_only_cf_river), median(combined_cf)),
  CF_p95 = c(quantile(legacy_cf_river, 0.95), quantile(fit_only_cf_river, 0.95), quantile(combined_cf, 0.95))
)
knitr::kable(cf_before_after_river, digits = 3, caption = "SPEC 1 before/after river correction factor convention check")
```

## A.2 Food Dilution RQ decomposition (legacy cumulative vs. corrected differential a.v/a.sa)

The Section 13 table above (SPEC 1, from the prior revision) shows that the **length**-slope convention fix changes the exposure correction factor. The volume/area-slope fix in this revision (SPEC 1b) is a separate, **hazard-side-only** effect: it does not touch `correction_factor()` or the EED at all, only the particle-trait alignment used inside pSSD++ (`a.v.*`, `a.sa.*`, `a.m.*`). To make that effect auditable, this section re-runs the pSSD++ hazard alignment and 1D risk characterization for each matrix with a "legacy" parameter set in which **only** `a.v`/`a.sa`/`a.m` are reverted to the pre-fix cumulative-slope values (`legacy_cumulative_av_params()`, `R/mp_risk_utils.R`) — holding the length slope, R.ave, exposure (EED), and everything else fixed — so the entire before/after RQ change in this table is attributable to the volume/area-slope convention alone.


```{r spec1b-decomposition-table}
spec1b_decomposition <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_legacy_river, Matrix = "River water", Case = "Legacy cumulative a.v/a.sa"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary,               Matrix = "River water", Case = "Corrected differential a.v/a.sa"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_legacy_sed,    Matrix = "Sediment",    Case = "Legacy cumulative a.v/a.sa"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_sed,           Matrix = "Sediment",    Case = "Corrected differential a.v/a.sa"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_legacy_ocean,  Matrix = "Ocean water", Case = "Legacy cumulative a.v/a.sa"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_ocean,         Matrix = "Ocean water", Case = "Corrected differential a.v/a.sa")
) |>
  dplyr::select(Matrix, Case, ERM, HCx, RQ_p50, RQ_p95, P_exceed) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Matrix, ERM, HCx, dplyr::desc(Case))

knitr::kable(
  spec1b_decomposition,
  digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3), # NA (not 0) here would make knitr::kable round(HCx, NA) -> NA; 0 is a no-op on the character columns
  caption = "SPEC 1b before/after Food Dilution and Tissue Translocation RQ decomposition: legacy cumulative a.v/a.sa (pre-fix) vs. corrected differential a.v/a.sa (this revision), holding exposure and the length-slope alignment fixed"
)

spec1b_food_hc5_ratio <- spec1b_decomposition |>
  dplyr::filter(ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5) |>
  dplyr::select(Matrix, Case, RQ_p50) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Case, values_from = RQ_p50) |>
  dplyr::mutate(collapse_factor = `Legacy cumulative a.v/a.sa` / `Corrected differential a.v/a.sa`)

knitr::kable(
  spec1b_food_hc5_ratio,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "SPEC 1b Food Dilution HC5 median-RQ collapse factor (legacy / corrected) by matrix"
)
```

The volume/area-slope correction is confined to the hazard alignment: exposure concentrations, the EED, and `combined_cf`/`combined_cf_sed`/`combined_cf_ocean` are numerically identical between the legacy and corrected rows above (they are not recomputed in this section). The magnitude of the collapse in the Food Dilution HC5 median RQ therefore isolates the volume-slope error described in SPEC 1b, consistent with the mean-particle-volume sensitivity calculation in the spec (a.v = 0.76 vs. 1.68 implying an ~4-6 million-fold difference in mean particle volume, and a comparable inverse effect on the Food Dilution threshold and RQ). **Correction (SPEC 3c):** Tissue Translocation is *not* expected to be insensitive to this fix overall — it is insensitive to the volume slope specifically (its dose model is not volume-weighted), but it *is* materially sensitive to the surface-area slope reverted in the same combined row above, because Tissue Translocation/oxidative-stress alignment is surface-area-weighted; see Section 14.1 for the row that isolates `a.sa` alone and the corrected narrative. **Sediment caveat (SPEC 1d):** the Sediment rows above are illustrative/non-quantitative — their exposure concentration is not a genuine particles/kg-dry-weight value (Section 11.3.0) — so while they are retained here to confirm the volume/area-slope-convention mechanism holds across matrices, the absolute RQ magnitudes for Sediment must not be read as real risk estimates (Section 11.4.0, 15.3).

## A.3 RQ decomposition — one-at-a-time convention reversions

Two convention fixes, made at different times, both change the Food Dilution risk quotient, for different reasons: (i) the exposure-side power-law **correction factor** (`correction_factor()`, Section 5.1) rescales the *measured concentration*; (ii) the hazard-side **length-slope alignment** (`alpha.freshwater`/`alpha.marine`/`alpha.sediment.freshwater` inside pSSD++, fixed in the prior revision) changes how toxicity endpoints are aligned to a common particle-size basis; and (iii) the hazard-side **volume/area-slope alignment** (`a.v.*`/`a.sa.*`/`a.m.*`, SPEC 1b, this revision) changes the polydisperse mean particle volume used by the Food Dilution dose model. This section isolates each of the three as a one-at-a-time sensitivity relative to the fully corrected river-water baseline, reverting exactly one piece to its legacy (pre-fix) form while holding the other two at their corrected values. River water is used as the representative matrix (the all-matrix table in Section 13.1 already shows (iii) holds for sediment and ocean water too).

```{r spec3b-decomp-exposure-cf-legacy}
# (i) Exposure correction factor reverted to legacy (cumulative-as-differential),
# hazard (haz) held at the fully corrected values. No pSSD rerun needed: this
# only recomputes the corrected-concentration draws with the legacy CF vector
# already computed above (A.1, legacy_cf_river).
set.seed(9202)
C_legacycf_draws <- monitoring |>
  dplyr::mutate(idx = dplyr::row_number()) |>
  tidyr::crossing(draw = seq_len(3000)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cf          = sample(legacy_cf_river, size = dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE),
    C_corrected = C_measured_pL * cf
  )
C_sample_median_legacycf <- C_legacycf_draws |>
  dplyr::group_by(sample_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(C_corr_med = stats::median(C_corrected), .groups = "drop")
eed_boot_legacycf_river <- bootstrap_eed(C_sample_median_legacycf$C_corr_med, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95))
set.seed(9307)
risk_summary_legacycf_river <- summarize_rq(draw_rq_mc1d(haz, eed_boot_legacycf_river$q50, n_risk = n_risk))
```

```{r spec3b-decomposition-table}
# (iii) reuses risk_summary_legacy_river from Section 13.1 (a.v/a.sa/a.m all
# reverted together, length alpha and exposure corrected); (iv, SPEC 3c) isolates
# a.sa alone. Both ERMs (Food Dilution and Tissue Translocation) are reported,
# since SPEC 3c found the prior Food-Dilution-only table masked how the a.sa
# reversion affects the surface-area-weighted Tissue Translocation ERM.
rq_decomp_river_raw <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary,                        Contribution_reverted = "None (fully corrected, this revision)"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_legacycf_river,         Contribution_reverted = "(i) Exposure correction factor -> legacy cumulative-as-differential"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_legacy_alpha_river,      Contribution_reverted = "(ii) Hazard length-slope alignment -> legacy cumulative-as-differential"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_legacy_river,           Contribution_reverted = "(iii) Hazard volume+area+mass-slope alignment -> legacy cumulative (SPEC 1b)"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_legacy_asa_river,        Contribution_reverted = "(iv) Hazard surface-area-slope alignment ONLY -> legacy cumulative (SPEC 3c)")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(HCx == 5) |>
  dplyr::select(ERM, Contribution_reverted, RQ_p50, RQ_p95, P_exceed)

rq_decomp_corrected_baseline <- rq_decomp_river_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(Contribution_reverted == "None (fully corrected, this revision)") |>
  dplyr::select(ERM, RQ_p50_corrected = RQ_p50)

rq_decomp_river <- rq_decomp_river_raw |>
  dplyr::left_join(rq_decomp_corrected_baseline, by = "ERM") |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio_vs_corrected = RQ_p50 / RQ_p50_corrected) |>
  dplyr::select(-RQ_p50_corrected) |>
  dplyr::arrange(ERM, dplyr::desc(Contribution_reverted == "None (fully corrected, this revision)"))

knitr::kable(
  rq_decomp_river, digits = 3,
  caption = "SPEC 3b/3c: River-water Food Dilution and Tissue Translocation HC5 RQ decomposition -- one-at-a-time reversion of each convention fix, relative to the fully corrected baseline (per ERM)"
)
```

```{r spec3b-decomposition-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
rq_decomp_plot <- rq_decomp_river |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Contribution_reverted = stringr::str_wrap(Contribution_reverted, width = 42),
    Contribution_reverted = factor(Contribution_reverted, levels = rev(unique(Contribution_reverted)))
  ) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = Contribution_reverted, y = RQ_p50, color = ERM)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  ggplot2::geom_pointrange(
    ggplot2::aes(ymin = RQ_p50, ymax = RQ_p95),
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 0.6, fatten = 2.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = ERM_PALETTE, name = "ERM") +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "HC5 median RQ (point), with p95 as the upper whisker [log10 scale]",
    title = "River-water RQ decomposition: one-at-a-time convention reversion",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = RQ = 1. Each row reverts exactly one convention fix, holding the others corrected.",
    caption = "Same data as the table above (rq_decomp_river)."
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.border    = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    plot.caption    = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50", hjust = 0)
  )

ggsave(rq_decomp_plot, filename = "figures/rq_decomp_plot.png", width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300)
rq_decomp_plot
```

Reading the table: the `ratio_vs_corrected` column is how much larger (or smaller) each ERM's HC5 median RQ becomes if *only* that one convention error were reintroduced, relative to that same ERM's own fully-corrected baseline. Because this is a `r n_boot`-replicate development-scale run (production budgets are ≥1000 per the deliverables checklist), the exact ratios should be treated as directionally informative rather than final, and re-checked at full budget before external release.

**SPEC 3c correction to the Tissue Translocation attribution.** Tissue Translocation P(RQ>1) at HC5 moves from `r round(tt_legacy$P_exceed * 100, 1)`% under the legacy (cumulative-as-differential) length-slope alignment to `r round(tt_now$P_exceed * 100, 1)`% under the corrected alignment, confirming the length-slope fix (prior revision) is one material driver of the Tissue Translocation shift. However, the volume+area+mass reversion also moves Tissue Translocation P(RQ>1) materially, from `r round(tt_legacy_av$P_exceed * 100, 1)`% (legacy) to `r round(tt_now$P_exceed * 100, 1)`% (corrected) — a change of this size is **not** "essentially unchanged," and a prior version of this narrative incorrectly claimed it was. Isolating the surface-area slope alone (a.sa reverted to legacy cumulative, a.v/a.m/alpha/exposure held corrected) reproduces most of that shift: P(RQ>1) is `r round(tt_legacy_asa$P_exceed * 100, 1)`% under the legacy a.sa alone, versus `r round(tt_now$P_exceed * 100, 1)`% corrected. This is mechanistically expected: unlike Food Dilution (volume-weighted), Tissue Translocation/oxidative-stress alignment is **surface-area-weighted**, so it is directly sensitive to the a.sa correction (cumulative a.sa ≈ 1.3 → differential a.sa ≈ 2.3 for river water; Section 13.1/7.2) in the same way Food Dilution is sensitive to a.v. Tissue Translocation is not literally insensitive to SPEC 1b — it is insensitive to the volume slope specifically (because dose is not volume-weighted) but sensitive to the area slope (because dose is area-weighted). **Corrected qualitative conclusion:** after both the length-slope and area-slope fixes, river-water Tissue Translocation HC5 is below threshold at the median (RQ ≈ `r round(tt_now$RQ_p50, 3)`, P(RQ>1) ≈ `r round(tt_now$P_exceed * 100, 1)`%), while Food Dilution (RQ ≈ `r round(fd_now$RQ_p50, 3)`, P(RQ>1) ≈ `r round(fd_now$P_exceed * 100, 1)`%) remains risk-dominant.


## Appendix B: C-PSD implementation validation

## B.1 Segur `PSD_fit.py` run on W2W particle-length PSDs, compared with the native R implementation

The native R C-PSD fit (`fit_cpsd_segur_r()`) and the Segur et al. (2026) reference implementation (`PSD_fit.py`, run below against the same W2W binned particle-length PSDs) are bit-identical after reconciling both to the identical populated-bin set (SPEC Q1: max|Δ*a*~cpsd~| = 8.44e-15, matching `n_bins` for all nine matrix × shape PSDs, asserted below); full method and comparison table in Appendix B.

```{r prepare-w2w-bins-for-segur-python, echo=FALSE}
segur_bins_from_fit <- function(psd_id, fit, shape_dimension = 3) {
  fit$bins |>
    dplyr::filter(n > 0, is.finite(L_low), is.finite(L_high), L_high > L_low) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      PSD_ID = psd_id,
      Low_size = L_low,
      High_size = L_high,
      Bin_concentration = n,
      shape_factor = 0,
      dimention = shape_dimension
    )
}

segur_python_bins <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  segur_bins_from_fit("W2W_river_all", cpsd_fit_all),
  segur_bins_from_fit("W2W_river_fragment", cpsd_fit_frag),
  segur_bins_from_fit("W2W_river_fiber", cpsd_fit_fiber, shape_dimension = 1),
  segur_bins_from_fit("W2W_sediment_all", cpsd_fit_sed_all),
  segur_bins_from_fit("W2W_sediment_fragment", cpsd_fit_sed_frag),
  segur_bins_from_fit("W2W_sediment_fiber", cpsd_fit_sed_fiber, shape_dimension = 1),
  segur_bins_from_fit("W2W_ocean_all", cpsd_fit_ocean_all),
  segur_bins_from_fit("W2W_ocean_fragment", cpsd_fit_ocean_frag),
  segur_bins_from_fit("W2W_ocean_fiber", cpsd_fit_ocean_fiber, shape_dimension = 1)
)
```

```{r compare-segur-python-r-fits, echo=FALSE}
# SPEC Q1 acceptance checks: (1) max(|delta_a_cpsd|) < 1e-6 across all nine
# matrix x shape PSDs, (2) R and Python agree on which bins were populated
# (n_bins_R == n_bins_Python). Both are asserted (not just reported) so a
# future data or algorithm change that reintroduces a binning mismatch fails
# loudly here rather than silently drifting.
q1_max_abs_delta_a_cpsd <- max(abs(segur_python_compare$delta_a_cpsd), na.rm = TRUE)
q1_n_bins_mismatch <- segur_python_compare |>
  dplyr::filter(R_n_bins != Python_n_bins | is.na(R_n_bins) != is.na(Python_n_bins))

    format(q1_max_abs_delta_a_cpsd, scientific = TRUE), "\n")

if (nrow(q1_n_bins_mismatch) > 0) {
  cat("SPEC Q1: n_bins mismatch remains for", nrow(q1_n_bins_mismatch), "PSD(s) -- documenting rather than silently failing:\n")
  print(q1_n_bins_mismatch |> dplyr::select(PSD_ID, R_n_bins, Python_n_bins, R_a_cpsd, Python_a_cpsd, delta_a_cpsd))
} else {

}

    q1_max_abs_delta_a_cpsd < 1e-6,
  "SPEC Q1 acceptance failed: n_bins mismatch between R and Python -- see printed diagnostic above" =
    nrow(q1_n_bins_mismatch) == 0
)
```

## Appendix C: Sediment (non-quantitative) and exploratory diagnostics

Sediment is excluded from the headline risk conclusion (Section 11) because its exposure concentration is not a genuine particles/kg-dry-weight value. The material below extends the sediment analysis for methods/illustrative purposes only -- none of it should be combined with the Section 11 exposure figures to produce a sediment risk quotient.

## C.1 sediment PSD-shift sensitivity (illustrative; production-gated)

This subsection implements `sediment_psd_shift_sensitivity()` (`R/mp_risk_utils.R`), which re-runs the full sediment hazard alignment (`matrix_function()` → `run_pssd_pipeline()` → `build_haz_df()`) across a grid of progressively finer sediment PSDs, representing continued in-situ fragmentation, and reports how the derived Food Dilution and Tissue Translocation HC5 respond as more particles fall below benthic bioaccessibility limits. A genuine hazard-side response (not merely a rescaled exposure number) requires this full re-run, because steepening the PSD changes the simulated particle-size population that pSSD++'s ingestible/translocatable size-gating operates on — i.e., it can change *which* species clear the bioaccessibility threshold and enter the SSD.

**Gating.** This sensitivity is gated on `sediment_concentration_is_quantitative` (currently `r sediment_concentration_is_quantitative`, SPEC 1d-i). While FALSE it is run as an illustrative/methods demonstration only — every row below is explicitly labeled non-quantitative and excluded from the risk conclusion, analogous to the existing single-slope↔piecewise CF bound (SPEC 2b, Section 13.3). It becomes a production sensitivity feeding the sediment RQ range only once that flag is set TRUE.

**What is *not* transplanted.** Thuy-Dung et al.'s *k*~frag~/shell-geometry fragmentation model is calibrated to polymer-coated-fertilizer prills with 7-year field data — a single, known-age, known-geometry polymer system — not the heterogeneous mixed-polymer sediment microplastics of unknown age sampled here. Rather than fit a kinetic rate that would not transfer to this dataset, the size-shift below is parameterized as an explicit, cited scenario grid: an added shift to the differential length/area/volume/mass slopes (`alpha`/`a.v`/`a.sa`/`a.m.sediment.freshwater`, positive-alpha convention — larger values are steeper/finer), applied identically across all four size metrics as a simplifying assumption (fragmentation is assumed to shift all size metrics proportionally).

```{r sediment-psd-shift-sensitivity}
# 0 = no shift (baseline -- an internal consistency check against
# Section 11.4's production sediment HC5, subject to Monte Carlo/parallel RNG
# noise since no fixed seed is threaded through PSSDplusplus's parallel
# workers); +0.75 and +1.5 = illustrative moderate/substantial in-situ
# fragmentation scenarios. Uses the *same* n_boot/sim/cv_uf/rmore_method as the
# production sediment call (Section 11.2/11.3) -- no analytical-budget change.
sed_psd_shift_grid <- c(0, 0.75, 1.5)

sed_psd_shift_tbl <- sediment_psd_shift_sensitivity(
  param_values_base = param_values_sed,
  slope_shift_grid  = sed_psd_shift_grid,
  tox_data_sed      = tox_data_sed,
  n_boot            = n_boot,
  cv_uf             = 0.5,
  rmore_method      = "lognormal",
  sim               = 30,
  num_cores         = parallel::detectCores() - 2,
  quantitative_flag = sediment_concentration_is_quantitative
)

knitr::kable(
  sed_psd_shift_tbl |> dplyr::filter(HCx == 5),
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste0(
    "SPEC 1e-ii: illustrative sediment PSD-shift sensitivity (HC5 only; particles/kg dw). is_quantitative = ",
    sediment_concentration_is_quantitative,
    " -- while FALSE, every row is non-quantitative/illustrative and excluded from the risk conclusion (SPEC 1d)."
  )
)
```

```{r sediment-psd-shift-inline, include=FALSE}
sed_shift_fd <- sed_psd_shift_tbl |> dplyr::filter(ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5) |> dplyr::arrange(slope_shift)
sed_shift_tt <- sed_psd_shift_tbl |> dplyr::filter(ERM == "Tissue Translocation", HCx == 5) |> dplyr::arrange(slope_shift)
sed_shift_fd_fold <- sed_shift_fd$HC_value_particles_kg[1] / sed_shift_fd$HC_value_particles_kg[nrow(sed_shift_fd)]
sed_shift_tt_fold <- sed_shift_tt$HC_value_particles_kg[1] / sed_shift_tt$HC_value_particles_kg[nrow(sed_shift_tt)]
```

Across the illustrative grid from no shift to the largest tested shift (`r max(sed_psd_shift_grid)`), the derived median Food Dilution HC5 changes by a factor of `r round(sed_shift_fd_fold, 2)`x and the Tissue Translocation HC5 by a factor of `r round(sed_shift_tt_fold, 2)`x (both relative to the unshifted grid point) — i.e., at this development-scale budget the rendered HC5 *rose* rather than fell as the illustrative PSD was shifted finer, the opposite of the direction the mechanism in Section 11.5.1 would naively suggest. **This is read as evidence of SSD instability, not as a directional finding.** The sediment benthic SSD is built from only `r dplyr::n_distinct(tox_data_sed$Species)` species; shifting which particles clear the ingestible/translocatable size gate can change *which* one or two species anchor the low-percentile HC5 extrapolation, and with this few species that anchor can swap non-monotonically rather than shift smoothly — exactly the small/unstable-SSD concern Thuy-Dung et al. (2026) raise as the motivation for tracking individual-species risk (Section 11.5.4) alongside a community HC5 extrapolated from so few species. **This table and plot remain non-quantitative** while `sediment_concentration_is_quantitative` is FALSE, regardless of direction: no number in this subsection should be combined with the Section 11.4 exposure figures to produce a sediment RQ, and the illustrative grid should not be read as showing that further fragmentation lowers sediment risk.


## C.2 time-varying bioaccessibility (documented; future enhancement)

The existing pSSD++ bioaccessibility alignment already used throughout this report (food dilution → gut-volume alignment; translocation truncated at the 500 µm upper tissue-translocation limit, both inside `run_pssd_pipeline()`/`PSSDplusplus::MC_sim_align_parallel()`) is the same machinery this extension would reuse — it is a size-dependent gate, not a new framework. **TODO (not implemented in this revision):** make that gate explicitly time-dependent by (1) parameterizing the sediment PSD shift in Section 11.5.2 as a function of residence time `t` rather than an unordered scenario index (e.g., a size-shift schedule Δα(t) informed by, but not equal to, Thuy-Dung et al.'s doubling-time concept — explicitly *not* their prill-specific *k*~frag~, per Section 11.5.2's non-transplant note); (2) re-running `run_pssd_pipeline()` at each time step exactly as Section 11.5.2 already does at each scenario point, so smaller-mouthed/smaller-gut benthic species progressively clear the `ingestible`/`translocatable` size gate as the bed fragments; (3) reporting HC5(*t*) and, where a genuine sediment concentration becomes available (SPEC 1d), RCR(*t*), as a trajectory rather than a single value. This is left as a clearly-scoped TODO rather than implemented here because it requires a defensible time axis (a residence-time or age-of-deposition estimate for this sediment dataset) that does not currently exist in the source data — fabricating one would misrepresent the method's evidentiary basis. Section 11.5.2's scenario grid is the same computational step without the time axis, and can be converted into this trajectory once residence-time data are available.

This water-sediment comparison is interpretive inference, not a new correction. Under Hoffman et al. (2026), sediment and water PSDs may be linked by size sorting: loss of larger dense particles from the water column should correspond to sediment enrichment in those sizes. The plot and table are retained as a coherence check to guide future transport-correction work.


# 15.5 C1 number-snapshot guardrail

The C1 consolidation pass (structure/presentation only; see `docs/CHANGELOG_hoffman_revisions.md`) must not change any live number. This chunk captures every headline value the C1 spec designates as protected -- river/sediment/ocean CF medians + 90% CIs, river/ocean EED q50/q95, the canonical 9-row C-PSD slope table, the SPEC Q1 max|delta a_cpsd|, the slope-structural-SD sensitivity grid, and river/ocean 1D + MC2D risk summaries -- into `data_output/c1_number_snapshot.json` the first time it renders (file does not yet exist), and on every subsequent render re-derives the same values and asserts they still match that baseline within 1e-8 (exact equality for integers/n_bins). A failure here means a structural edit silently moved a number and must be treated as a stop-and-fix, not a value to update casually -- see `docs/CHANGELOG_hoffman_revisions.md` before touching the baseline file itself.

```{r c1-number-snapshot}
c1_snapshot_path <- file.path(proj_root, "data_output", "c1_number_snapshot.json")

build_c1_snapshot <- function() {
  slope_tbl <- this_study_length_alpha |>
    dplyr::filter(Source == "This study matrix/shape") |>
    dplyr::arrange(PSD_ID) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      PSD_ID, Matrix, Shape,
      a_cpsd = round(a_cpsd, 10), a_psd = round(a_psd, 10),
      lod_low_um = round(lod_low_um, 6), lod_high_um = round(lod_high_um, 6),
      n_bins = as.integer(n_bins)
    )

  rq_tbl <- function(x) x |> dplyr::arrange(ERM, HCx) |>
    dplyr::transmute(ERM, HCx, P_exceed = round(P_exceed, 10),
                      RQ_p50 = round(RQ_p50, 10), RQ_p95 = round(RQ_p95, 10))

  mc2d_tbl <- function(x) x |> dplyr::arrange(ERM, HCx) |>
    dplyr::transmute(ERM, HCx, P_exceed_med = round(P_exceed_med, 10),
                      RQ_p50_med = round(RQ_p50_med, 10), RQ_p95_med = round(RQ_p95_med, 10))

  list(
    cf_river  = list(p50 = unname(round(median(combined_cf), 10)),
                      p05 = unname(round(quantile(combined_cf, 0.05), 10)),
                      p95 = unname(round(quantile(combined_cf, 0.95), 10))),
    cf_sed    = list(p50 = unname(round(median(combined_cf_sed), 10)),
                      p05 = unname(round(quantile(combined_cf_sed, 0.05), 10)),
                      p95 = unname(round(quantile(combined_cf_sed, 0.95), 10))),
    cf_ocean  = list(p50 = unname(round(median(combined_cf_ocean), 10)),
                      p05 = unname(round(quantile(combined_cf_ocean, 0.05), 10)),
                      p95 = unname(round(quantile(combined_cf_ocean, 0.95), 10))),
    eed_river = list(q50 = unname(round(median(eed_boot$q50), 10)),
                      q95 = unname(round(median(eed_boot$q95), 10))),
    eed_ocean = list(q50 = unname(round(median(eed_boot_ocean$q50), 10)),
                      q95 = unname(round(median(eed_boot_ocean$q95), 10))),
    slope_table         = slope_tbl,
    spec_q1_max_delta    = unname(round(q1_max_abs_delta_a_cpsd, 10)),
    hoffman_sensitivity = hoffman_slope_sensitivity |>
      dplyr::arrange(structural_sd, ERM) |>
      dplyr::transmute(ERM, structural_sd, P_exceed_med = round(P_exceed_med, 10),
                        RQ_p50_med = round(RQ_p50_med, 10), RQ_p95_med = round(RQ_p95_med, 10)),
    rq_1d_river  = rq_tbl(risk_summary),
    rq_1d_sed    = rq_tbl(risk_summary_sed),
    rq_1d_ocean  = rq_tbl(risk_summary_ocean),
    mc2d_river   = mc2d_tbl(mc2d_summary),
    mc2d_ocean   = mc2d_tbl(mc2d_ocean_summary)
  )
}

snap_current <- build_c1_snapshot()

if (n_boot < 1000) {
  message("C1 guardrail: SKIPPED -- n_boot = ", n_boot, " (< 1000, dev-scale iteration render). ",
          "The byte-identical number check is only meaningful at the production budget; ",
          "re-render with n_boot = 1000 before treating this as a release-gate pass.")
} else if (!file.exists(c1_snapshot_path)) {
  jsonlite::write_json(snap_current, c1_snapshot_path, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15, pretty = TRUE)
  message("C1 guardrail: baseline snapshot written to ", c1_snapshot_path,
          " (this is the pre-C1 baseline -- do not regenerate once C1 edits begin).")
} else {
  snap_baseline <- jsonlite::read_json(c1_snapshot_path, simplifyVector = TRUE)

  compare_numeric <- function(cur, base, path = "") {
    if (is.list(cur) && !is.data.frame(cur)) {
      nm <- names(cur)
      unlist(lapply(nm, function(n) compare_numeric(cur[[n]], base[[n]], paste0(path, "$", n))))
    } else if (is.data.frame(cur)) {
      base_df <- as.data.frame(base)
      stopifnot2 <- vapply(setdiff(names(cur), c("PSD_ID","Matrix","Shape","ERM","HCx")), function(col) {
        max(abs(cur[[col]] - base_df[[col]]), na.rm = TRUE)
      }, numeric(1))
      setNames(stopifnot2, paste0(path, "$", names(stopifnot2)))
    } else {
      setNames(abs(as.numeric(cur) - as.numeric(base)), path)
    }
  }

  diffs <- unlist(compare_numeric(snap_current, snap_baseline))
  tol <- 1e-8
  bad <- diffs[!is.na(diffs) & diffs >= tol]

  if (length(bad) > 0) {
    print(sort(bad, decreasing = TRUE))
    # Diagnostic print() output can be lost if the render halts before the
    # chunk's buffer flushes; also write it to a plain file so a failure is
    # debuggable from the last render alone.
    writeLines(
      c(paste0("C1 guardrail FAILURE -- ", length(bad), " value(s) exceeded tol = ", tol),
        capture.output(print(sort(bad, decreasing = TRUE))),
        "",
        "-- current --",
        capture.output(str(snap_current, max.level = 2)),
        "",
        "-- baseline --",
        capture.output(str(snap_baseline, max.level = 2))),
      file.path(proj_root, "data_output", "c1_guardrail_failure_diagnostic.txt")
    )
  }
  message("C1 guardrail: max|delta| across ", length(diffs), " tracked values = ",
          format(max(diffs, na.rm = TRUE), scientific = TRUE))
  stopifnot(
    "C1 guardrail FAILED: a structural edit changed a protected number -- see printed diagnostic above" =
      length(bad) == 0
  )
  message("C1 guardrail: all tracked values match the pre-C1 baseline within ", tol, ".")
}
```
